13:20.race_name: Turners Novices' Hurdle (Grade 1) (Registered As The Baring Bingham Novices' Hurdle) (GBB Race)

runners.comment: Looked good when winning a Huntingdon Listed event last time; one of the key British hopes
runners.name: Act Of Innocence
runners.spotlight: Considered a Supreme hope at the start of the term and he did nothing to dispel those thoughts when impressing on hurdles debut in a Newbury maiden (about 2m, soft) in November; surprisingly turned over by a 3yo over that C&D (good) one month later but firmly back on track when sent up in trip to comfortably land a Huntingdon Listed event (about 2m4f, soft) last time; his trainer used that race as a stepping stone to Cheltenham Festival glory for Shishkin in 2020 and this one commands plenty of respect.

runners.comment: Just picked off in Leopardstown Grade 1 last month; new trip; very strong claims
runners.name: Ballyfad
runners.spotlight: Unbeaten in a point and two bumpers before easily winning a Leopardstown maiden hurdle (2m, yielding; strong in the market) in December; fine effort when claimed on the line in a Grade 1 over that C&D (heavy) at the start of last month, with King Rasko Grey a close-up third, and his pedigree suggests this new trip will be no problem; very strong claims for his powerful yard.

runners.comment: Won his last two; on the up for last year's winning yard; impossible to rule out
runners.name: Bossman Jack
runners.owner: M W Lake & Exors Of The Late N W Lake
runners.spotlight: Bumper winner who was off the mark on his second attempt over hurdles when winning a Ffos Las novice in January; heavy odds-on but he still impressed when easily defying a penalty at Chepstow (also 2m, soft) last month; dam won over this trip in a light hurdling career; not far away on the figures for last year's winning stable and he's impossible to rule out.

runners.comment: Improved in handicaps since tongue tied; stiff assignment this time; now had wind surgery
runners.name: Came From Nowhere
runners.spotlight: Bumper winner who arrives here via the handicap route, improving once a tongue-tie was fitted to win at Hereford (about 2m4f) in December and Ascot (about 2m3f, also soft) in January; latter was a comfortable career best (wind surgery since) but this is a different test altogether.

runners.comment: Third in 2m5f Grade 2 here last time; useful sort but that form still leaves him short
runners.name: Fortune Timmy
runners.spotlight: Won hurdles debut at Fontwell (2m3f) in October and by a wide margin at same track (2m2f, again good to soft) in December; third in a Grade 2 on the New course here (about 2m5f; Taurus Bay second) was another good effort; that form still leaves him with something to find, however.

runners.comment: 3rd behind Sober on stable debut in January; needs more but still early days
runners.name: Free Spirit
runners.spotlight: Debut second at Auteuil (2m2f, heavy) in October 2024 and clung on at Dieppe (2m1f, soft) in June 2025; interestingly pitched into Grade 2 on stable debut at Punchestown (about 2m, soft; 9-2) in January, but that third of three behind Sober needs building on; very early days and this new trip might help.

runners.comment: Looked good on his first two starts but limitations were exposed last time; up in trip
runners.name: Hurricane Pat
runners.spotlight: Won his first two over hurdles, readily justifying the odds in Sandown maiden (2m, good to soft) in November before impressing in a Listed event over that C&D (soft, Soldier Reeves second) the following month; paid for trying to match it with the winner when firmly put in his place at Haydock last time, however, and that seemed to expose his limitations; goes up in trip.

runners.comment: 4-4 since back over hurdles; gritty G1 win latest; sort who won't go down without a fight
runners.name: Ill Sort That
runners.spotlight: 100-1 and borderline tailed off in a Cork maiden hurdle in December 2024 but he subsequently turned into a quality bumper performer and has taken it up a notch since resuming his career over hurdles, unbeaten in four including Navan Grade 3 (2m, soft to heavy) in November and when repeating forcing tactics in Naas Grade 1 (2m4f, soft; Sortudo second, Saint Baco behind) two months ago; won't find it easy to dominate this field but his gritty attitude was admirable last time and he likely won't go down without a fight.

runners.breeder: S A R L Mm Stud
runners.comment: Just behind Ballyfad in G1 last time; up in trip and he's Townend's pick; hugely respected
runners.name: King Rasko Grey
runners.spotlight: Comfortably got the better of Shuttle Diplomacy when winning a Limerick maiden (soft to heavy) on hurdles debut in late December and took the rise in class well when a close third in Leopardstown Grade 1 (also 2m, heavy; Ballyfad just ahead) at the start of February; should stay this far and he's Paul Townend's pick from a choice of six Willie Mullins runners; yard has a strong record in this race and he has to be on the shortlist.

runners.comment: 2nd to No Drama This End last time; work to do but he's the sort to outrun his likely odds
runners.name: Klimt Madrik
runners.spotlight: Chasing type who followed a solid hurdles debut in October by stepping up to win a Newbury novice (about 2m5f, soft) one month later; showed a good attitude that day and it was a fine effort when chasing home No Drama This End in the Grade 1 Challow over that C&D (good) towards the end of December; has work to do to turn those tables but he's the sort to outrun his likely odds.

runners.comment: Off the mark last time; new trip may unlock more and he's impossible to rule out
runners.name: Laurets dEstruval
runners.spotlight: Runner-up in sole French outing; 12 months off before second of 17 at Limerick (heavy) and he made no mistake when short odds at Thurles (also 2m, soft) last month; Paul Townend has jumped ship but it's impossible to know where the ceiling of his ability lies and this new trip may unlock more.

runners.comment: Made it 3-3 over hurdles in Grade 1 last time; the leading British hope; huge player
runners.name: No Drama This End
runners.owner: McNeill Family And Chris & Giles Barber
runners.spotlight: Impressively rewarded market support on bumper debut at Warwick last term before midfield in the Champion Bumper at last year's Cheltenham Festival; quickly established himself as the leading British-based hope for this race when laughing at a good one in a C&D Grade 2 in November before following up in the same grade at Sandown (2m4f, also soft) the following month; merely needed to be nudged along to make his Grade 1 breakthrough in the Challow at Newbury (good) in December and holds strong claims of following in the footsteps of The New Lion, who won that race before taking this last season.

runners.comment: Running respectably but his form leaves him short of the required standard
runners.name: Riskaway
runners.spotlight: Beat Zeus Power (improved since) when drawing well clear on hurdles debut at Thurles (good to yielding) in November; consistent on heavy when second to leading BetMGM Cup fancy Storm Heat at Limerick (also 2m4f) and fourth in 2m6f Leopardstown Grade 1; those efforts still leave him with a bit to find.

runners.comment: Market drifter when disappointing in Grade 1 last time; Paul Townend has jumped ship
runners.name: Saint Baco
runners.spotlight: Sent off odds-on, despite some unease in the betting, when beating a big field on his stable debut at Navan (2m, soft to heavy) in December and he was a notable market drifter when 9-2 and weakening over this sort of trip in a Naas Grade 1 (soft) fought out by I'll Sort That and Sortudo two months ago; Paul Townend, who was on board last time, has deserted him.

runners.breeder: E A R L Elevage Des Loges
runners.comment: Good bumper horse who's resurgent in a tongue-tie; won last time; not ruled out
runners.name: Shuttle Diplomacy
runners.spotlight: Won a Limerick Listed bumper two years ago and a cracking effort when third in the Champion Bumper (good to soft; Sortudo and No Drama This End behind) at last season's Cheltenham Festival; disappointed on first two starts over hurdles but he rediscovered his groove in a newly fitted tongue-tie when second to King Rasko Grey at Limerick (2m, soft to heavy) in December before beating 15 others to win at Naas (about 2m2f, heavy) last time; this forecast better ground should be fine and he's not one to dismiss lightly.

runners.comment: Probably lucky to win Grade 1 in December but that was still a cracking effort; big player
runners.name: Skylight Hustle
runners.spotlight: Won his only point but couldn't justify favouritism for a second time when beaten in his sole bumper; solid start over hurdles when second of 20 in a Gowran maiden (heavy) in November and his wide-margin win at Fairyhouse (yielding to soft) three weeks later contained a sprinkling of stardust; fortunate when left clear just after the last in Leopardstown Grade 1 (also 2m, yielding) in December; that still continued his upward trajectory and, while this new trip asks a small question on pedigree, he has to be seriously considered.

runners.comment: Group class on the Flat and he's 2-2 over hurdles; who knows how high he can fly
runners.name: Sober
runners.owner: Oti Racing & The Why Knot Partnership
runners.spotlight: Group class for Andre Fabre on the Flat and his win in last year's Queen Alexandra (good to firm) at Royal Ascot for this yard was sandwiched between two hurdle wins, in a Killarney novice (2m4f, yielding) in May and a triumphant comeback in Punchestown Grade 2 (about 2m, soft to heavy) two months ago despite drifting in the market; can likely fly higher in this sphere, particularly when his hurdling tightens up, and he's a fascinating contender.

runners.comment: Looks to have his work cut out on all known form
runners.name: Soldier Reeves
runners.spotlight: Made a winning debut over hurdles here (about 2m, soft; first-time tongue-tie) in November; readily brushed aside by Hurricane Pat at Sandown the following month, however, and probably flattered to get closer to that rival when soundly beaten at Haydock last time; goes up in trip with work to do.

runners.comment: Runner-up in Grade 1 at Naas two months ago on latest start; likely to run well again
runners.name: Sortudo
runners.spotlight: Finished mid-division in last season's Champion Bumper at the Cheltenham Festival but he was useful in that sphere and beat I'll Sort That by 12l when making all at Fairyhouse in April; got off to the perfect start over hurdles when comfortably winning a Cork maiden (2m, yielding to soft; first-time hood) in November but found his old rival I'll Sort That too strong when second in a Naas Grade 1 (2m4f, soft) two months ago; likely to run well again.

runners.comment: Just denied in Grade 2 here last time but that form still leaves him with a bit to find
runners.name: Taurus Bay
runners.spotlight: Point winner (3m, yielding) who made it 2-2 over hurdles (2m, good to soft/soft) in three-runner novice at Aintree in December; only just denied over this sort of trip in soft-ground Grade 2 on the New course here in January; has quite a plucky attitude but that form leaves him with something to find.

runners.comment: Won a handicap last time; needs more but that's not inconceivable from this yard
runners.name: Walks In June
runners.spotlight: Point winner who was strong in the market when he made a winning hurdles debut at Limerick (about 2m, yielding to soft) in October; limitations were seemingly exposed in a heavy-ground Grade 3 at Navan next time but he doubled his tally in this sphere when taking a Leopardstown handicap (also about 2m4f, good to yielding) in late December; will need more but that's not inconceivable for a yard whose runners can rarely be dismissed at this meeting.

runners.comment: Improving sort who goes back up in trip after winning his last two; could go well
runners.name: Zeus Power
runners.spotlight: Safely held when second to Riskaway at Thurles (2m4f, good to yielding) but improved since; followed a wide-margin win there (yielding to soft) by responding well for pressure to score at Navan (also 2m, soft to heavy); the step back up in trip is probably of little concern and he might surprise a few.

14:00.race_name: Brown Advisory Novices' Chase (Grade 1) (Registered As The Broadway Novices' Chase) (GBB Race)

runners.comment: G3 winner last time in a slow-motion finish; needs to improve and most form in deep ground
runners.name: Argento Boy
runners.spotlight: Winner of both completed chase starts, including in slow-motion finish to Naas Grade 3 in January (extended 3m, heavy); will stay but has more to find on ratings than most and bulk of his form has come on testing ground.

runners.comment: Impressive before DRF defeat and a player on form if he stays; tongue-tie fitted
runners.name: Final Demand
runners.spotlight: Sole defeat over hurdles came at this meeting last year (third to The New Lion in Turners) and lost his undefeated record over fences when just over 12l third to Kaid d'Authie in Grade 1 at the Dublin Racing Festival (extended 2m5f, soft); previous wins were impressive and he's a big player on form, but that defeat and the addition of a tongue-tie are concerns.

runners.comment: Outstayed the runner-up in a 3m chase last time; stiff task upped to G1 level
runners.name: Joystick
runners.spotlight: Big improvement on third chase start when beating Slade Steel at Navan in January (3m, soft to heavy); runner-up had his measure that day before stamina came into it, so it's hard to imagine he is up to this higher level.

runners.comment: Impressed with jumping and attitude in Grade 1 at DRF last time; leading player
runners.name: Kaid dAuthie
runners.spotlight: Has improved drastically for fences, finishing second to Kitzbuhel on debut before winning at Fairyhouse (2m6f, yielding) and in Grade 1 at Dublin Racing Festival (extended 2m5f, soft; beat Western Fold by just over 4l); impressed with his jumping and how he stuck to his task last time, attributes you need for this race, and he sets the standard on form; leading player.

runners.comment: Won G1 at Kempton on Boxing Day but jumps right and others might have improved past him
runners.name: Kitzbuhel
runners.spotlight: Set the early standard in this division, beating Kaid d'Authie on chase debut then winning Grade 1 Kauto Star at Kempton on Boxing Day (3m, good); jumped right before unseating in Sandown Grade 1 last time, and the worries today are going left-handed plus the sense that others have improved past him.

runners.comment: Wide-margin winner at Leopardstown over Christmas; opts for a G1 rather than handicaps
runners.name: Koktail Divin
runners.spotlight: Second to Romeo Coolio and Oscars Brother on first two chase starts before impressing when winning an often-indicative race at Leopardstown over Christmas (extended 2m5f, yielding) by 21l; looked a leading contender for a handicap this week but yard instead opts to tackle this Grade 1.

runners.comment: Somewhat fortunate Thyestes Chase winner last time; needs to improve again
runners.name: Now Is The Hour
runners.spotlight: Second-season novice who has improved significantly of late, winning Thyestes Chase at Gowran Park (3m1f handicap, heavy) in January; something of a fortunate winner that day and needs to improve again.

runners.comment: Won 3m Grade 2s on each of his last two starts and is one to consider each-way
runners.name: Oscars Brother
runners.spotlight: Progressive over fences, winning soft-ground 3m Grade 2s at Punchestown in November (beat Koktail Divin) and Navan in February (by 6l from The Wallpark) on his last two starts; has a better chance on form for his two-horse trainer than double-figure odds suggest; one to consider each-way.

runners.comment: Smart form over fences but needs to improve significantly moving into Grade 1 company
runners.name: Predators Gold
runners.spotlight: Smart novice hurdler in 2023-24, then missed over a year; similar form over fences, winning a maiden at Navan (extended 2m4f, soft to heavy) in December from Slade Steel, but needs to improve significantly.

runners.comment: Three G1 wins over fences; hiked in trip now, with a hood added in the hope he will settle
runners.name: Romeo Coolio
runners.spotlight: Champion Bumper second and Supreme Novices' third at last two Cheltenham Festivals; 4-4 over fences, winning three Grade 1s, but raced lazily in Irish Arkle (2m1f, soft) last time which has brought about this hike in trip; possibly the most talented horse in the race, but the trip is a real unknown and the fitting of a hood suggests even his connections have their doubts.

runners.comment: Won again at Thurles in December, in a warm handicap; still a way off Grade 1 standard
runners.name: Rushmount
runners.spotlight: Improved to win a handicap at Thurles (all wins there) in December (extended 2m5f, yielding); that has worked out but his form is still well off Grade 1 standard and he missed the Dublin Racing Festival due to coughing.

runners.comment: Dual Grade 2 winner but jumping has tended to be a sticking point; looks up against it
runners.name: Salver
runners.spotlight: Dual Grade 2 winner at about 3m over fences, at Sandown (good to soft) and Windsor (soft) in December/January; jumping again not fluent last time, despite added cheekpieces (retained), and he has his work cut out in this.

runners.comment: Second in Grade 1 on Boxing Day but not seen since and needs to build on that run
runners.name: Thomas Mor
runners.spotlight: Fifth in 2023 Albert Bartlett here for David Pipe; finally built on that when second to Kitzbuhel in Kauto Star on Boxing Day (3m, good); needs to improve on that and an abscess meant he missed an engagement at Ascot 25 days ago.

runners.comment: Looks to be Britain's best hope but may find one or two too good
runners.name: Wendigo
runners.spotlight: Fifth in last year's Albert Bartlett here and very smart form over fences, winning Grade 2 at Newbury in November (2m4f, good to soft); easy winner of novice at Ayr (3m, soft) 41 days ago and looks the best of the British hopes, although he may find one or two too good unless he improves again.

runners.comment: Progressive last summer and good 2nd to Kaid d'Authie at DRF; enters each-way calculations
runners.name: Western Fold
runners.spotlight: Progressive last summer, winning the Galway Plate (extended 2m6f, good), and he beat subsequent Savills Chase winner Affordale Fury at Gowran Park in October (2m4f, yielding to soft); good second to Kaid d'Authie at Dublin Racing Festival last time and enters each-way calculations.

runners.breeder: Southeast B/S O Hickey & L Gleeson
runners.comment: Runner-up at last year's Festival and G2 winner last time; may be better on testing ground
runners.name: The Big Westerner
runners.spotlight: Second (beaten favourite) in last year's Albert Bartlett; off the mark over fences in mares' Grade 2 novice at Limerick over Christmas (extended 2m6f, soft to heavy); improvement required, even with the sex allowance, and she was withdrawn on 'unsuitable' yielding ground in November.

14:40.race_name: BetMGM Cup Handicap Hurdle (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)

runners.comment: Big runs in Grade 1 novice races, including 2m5f here; cheekpieces for this handicap debut
runners.name: The Yellow Clay
runners.spotlight: Four-timer as a novice last season culminated in 2m4f Grade 1 at Naas, which he followed with second over 2m5f at this meeting (gave The New Lion plenty to think about); took a heavy fall at Punchestown in May, beaten at 8-15 in November (fair second) and failed to shine in Grade 1 at Christmas (notwithstanding the near 3m trip) so he's on a recovery mission, but last season can't be forgotten yet; cheekpieces go on for this handicap debut.

runners.comment: 11yo; second and third in the last two runnings of this race, which is quite something
runners.name: Ballyadam
runners.spotlight: Fifth in two editions of the County Hurdle here before his second and third in the last two runnings of this race, which is quite something; has a 1lb higher mark than last year; well held in his only hurdle race this term but placed in Flat maidens either side, and has to be in place calculations.

runners.breeder: S & G Kinast & Haras De La Rousseliere
runners.comment: Classy; stacks of encouragement for this sort of trip; bright prospects in second handicap
runners.name: Storm Heart
runners.spotlight: Lightly raced 6yo who was Triumph favourite here two years ago, below form in fifth; ran well in all other starts over hurdles, including a Grade 1 second earlier as juvenile, second of 18 in a big 2m handicap last February (made up a lot of ground) and wins on both runs this term; his only attempt at 2m4f was a stylish win on penultimate outing and his runs over shorter give stacks of encouragement for this sort of trip; the ground won't be so testing but he surely has bright prospects back up in trip in only his second handicap.

runners.breeder: E Aubree & Mrs J Goffin Van Aken
runners.comment: Has proved himself here and it will be no shock if this one is on the premises
runners.name: Lucky Place
runners.owner: Mrs G Van Geest & M George
runners.spotlight: Fourth in this in 2024 and last season's two Grade 2 wins included one at this track, before 3m experiment in Grade 1 Stayers' did not work out; chasing on first two starts this term before a respectable third to bright hope in Grade 2 hurdle here; Nicky Henderson's hurdlers so often run well in the Festival handicaps (one under Brian Hughes won the Pertemps Final last year) and it will be no shock if this one is on the premises.

runners.comment: Creditable fifth in last year's Grade 1 Stayers' here but he's not really sparked since
runners.name: Buddy One
runners.owner: E Lynch & T C Quinn & John J McGrath
runners.spotlight: Third in the 2m4f Martin Pipe at this meeting in 2023; creditable fifth in last year's Grade 1 Stayers' here but he's not really sparked since, including over fences; 6lb lower now than his peak British mark; equipped with cheekpieces on latest outing (stiff task) and today.

runners.comment: More to prove over this trip; makes his handicap debut aged nine, with first headgear
runners.name: Farren Glory
runners.spotlight: Won Grade 1 novice in 2023 and a beginners' chase in November 2024; only supporting roles in Graded events since, not far off Storm Heart on latest (2m, heavy); more to prove over this trip, and although he did win a 2023 maiden over an extended 2m3f, his 2m6f run last February (absent 350 days afterwards) does not convince; handicap debut aged nine, with first headgear.

runners.comment: Fifth in this race last year but he's higher in the weights today and is now an 11yo
runners.name: Colonel Mustard
runners.owner: Mrs A Frost & P G Davies & R H Fowler
runners.spotlight: Two races this autumn (one a 2m4f Grade 2 from The Yellow Clay) were his first wins for ages and he wasn't disgraced on latest outing; third in the 2022 County and fifth in this race last year in his only two handicaps at this meeting, but he's higher in the weights today and is now an 11yo, so can't be the percentage call.

runners.comment: Marked step up in trip is an interesting move; proven big-race performer, including here
runners.name: Puturhandstogether
runners.spotlight: It was never in doubt once his jockey pressed the button in last season's Fred Winter at this meeting (2m, good to soft) and much the same when he landed a huge pot in the Irish Cesarewitch on Flat (2m1f) in September; whether he's on a good mark is an issue but he may have found 2m at Listowel sharper than ideal when runner-up in September and this marked step up in trip is an interesting move; big-race performer who has to be given a close look.

runners.comment: Big talking horse at 2025 Festival; neck 2nd at Aintree (2m4f; 9lb higher today) in April
runners.name: Kopeck De Mee
runners.spotlight: Deafening, ex-French talking horse when favourite for the Martin Pipe at this meeting last year on debut for Willie Mullins, only to jump horribly in the early stages and hoist the white flag from two out; quickly proved that was all wrong when beaten a neck in big-field 2m4f handicap at Aintree (9lb higher today) but fell at the last when way off the pace on chase debut in December on his only start since; it's hard to know which version will turn up.

runners.breeder: Mrs J Rainer Mr F Jereczek & Mr Rainer
runners.comment: Second to a fine prospect here on New Year's Day; on his way back and bold show likely
runners.name: Jingko Blue
runners.spotlight: Unseated last February in his third chase but won the previous two and that form makes this hurdles mark look highly tempting; second to a fine prospect over hurdles here on New Year's Day (Lucky Place third) suggested he's on his way back; bold show likely for a top trainer with three solid candidates.

runners.comment: Back up 8lb after his 2m5f Lanzarote revival but he is firmly back on the radar
runners.name: Iberico Lord
runners.spotlight: Bagged two big 2m handicaps (here and at Newbury) in the mud during his 2023-24 campaign; had a spell in the wilderness but dropped back down the weights prior to scoring with major authority in the 2m5f Lanzarote at Kempton (good; 22-1) two months ago; back up 8lb but also firmly back on the radar.

runners.comment: Competitive in all completed handicaps over this sort of trip; won three but needs better
runners.name: Guard Duty
runners.spotlight: Not the greatest jumper and he comes from the back, which risks trouble in running, but competitive in all six of his completed handicaps over this sort of trip; won three of them, in just a four-runner race at Doncaster on latest start, though, and further improvement is needed.

runners.comment: Needs improvement but represents Mullins and far from fully exposed; first-time headgear
runners.name: Chart Topper
runners.owner: Aisling Byrne & Paul Raleigh & Matthew Cunningham
runners.spotlight: His four handicaps were over longer trips, notably when third at the Galway festival (extended 2m6f, good) last August; hampered and pulled up here in October, before falling in a narrow lead two out in 3m Pertemps qualifier at Haydock (20-1) last month; needs improvement and better luck but represents Willie Mullins and is far from fully exposed; first-time headgear too.

runners.breeder: R D & Mrs J S Chugg
runners.comment: Needs a close look, particularly given Dan Skelton's fine record in handicap hurdles here
runners.name: Kateira
runners.spotlight: First two runs (November) were her best from this season and she didn't shine back in handicaps on last two outings; however, her 2m4f win in a big-field handicap at 2024 Aintree festival should not be forgotten and she also ran well in Graded/Listed contests for most of last term; needs a close look, particularly given Dan Skelton's fine record in handicap hurdles at this meeting.

runners.comment: More is needed but from top yard and he's a dark horse with this big step up in trip
runners.name: Sony Bill
runners.spotlight: Two hurdle wins in France in spring 2024; yet to score for Willie Mullins after five attempts but they were all major races (7-1 when soundly beaten in the Fred Winter here last March) and he showed plenty of ability in 4yo Grade 1 at Punchestown last May; sole run since was in a top handicap last month; more is needed but he's a dark horse with this big step up in trip.

runners.comment: Unraced beyond 2m1f; plenty to prove in this search for a big career best
runners.name: Give It To Me Oj
runners.spotlight: Has set the pace in small fields; won six (four over hurdles, two on Flat) of seven starts in a golden spell last February-October, the final leg in a conditions event at this track; soundly beaten on both starts since (admittedly no chance in Grade 1 latest) and unraced beyond 2m1f, leaving him with plenty to prove in this search for a big career best.

runners.comment: Landed a notable prize in October but failed to show his form in his three starts since
runners.name: Rambo T
runners.spotlight: Landed a notable prize at Chepstow (near 2m4f, good; 3lb higher today) in October but failed to show his form in his three starts since; Sean Bowen rides him for the first time since Chepstow; he'd still be a surprise winner.

runners.comment: Won in October and was soft ground an excuse in November, but he's an 11yo
runners.name: Dargiannini
runners.spotlight: A 9yo won it in 2019 but it's stretching the imagination to see this 11yo prevail, even though he did so at Uttoxeter (2m4f, good) in October and soft ground was a valid excuse at Newbury (2m4f) in November; off since.

runners.comment: Bold shows at last two Festivals; not so good this season; a rare run without equipment
runners.name: Franciscan Rock
runners.spotlight: Fifth when 50-1 in this race in 2024 (1lb higher today) and 20l sixth when 80-1 for the Grade 1 Stayers' in 2025, close up turning for home on both occasions; not so good this season and this is a rare run without tongue-tie or other headgear; not entirely dismissed, though.

runners.comment: Sixth in this last year off 1lb higher in his third handicap; 2nd over fences last time
runners.name: Beckett Rock
runners.spotlight: Sixth in this last year off 1lb higher in his third handicap; chasing on last four starts, with the latest (second in a handicap) easily his best effort in that sphere, so he's of renewed interest even if he does not look the first string on jockey bookings for his highly respected stable.

runners.comment: Third in the Cesarewitch (second favourite) in October; 4th in a hot 2m4f handicap hurdle
runners.name: Bunting
runners.spotlight: Raced freely when 12-1 in this last year and was pulled up; a maiden hurdle in December 2023 remains his last win and he's not been consistent, but such performances as his Flat third in the Cesarewitch (second favourite; plenty went wrong) in October and fourth of 16 in a hot 2m4f handicap hurdle at Leopardstown in December show that he can still be competitive on his day.

runners.comment: No impact on last three outings; latest (11 days ago) was after four months off
runners.name: Minella Rescue
runners.spotlight: Ran well over about 3m on most starts last March-June, including 50-1 second in substandard Grade 1 novice at Aintree; took an age to warm up in that race, however, which makes this trip look against him, and no impact on last three outings; latest (11 days ago) was after four months off.

runners.comment: Maiden; cheekpieces on for leading yard on handicap debut; there are straws to clutch at
runners.name: Forty Coats
runners.spotlight: Point and bumper winner; 0-6 record as hurdler includes three seconds in maidens last winter before an excellent 15l fourth at 150-1 in the Grade 1 Turners here (2m5f, good to soft) last March; way below form in maidens on his two starts this winter (third at 4-9 last time) but the cheekpieces go on for his leading yard on handicap debut; there are straws to clutch at.

runners.comment: 2m4f non-handicap win with first-time blinkers (kept since) at Clonmel last June
runners.name: HMS Seahorse
runners.spotlight: Fourth in the Fred Winter here in 2022 but beaten 20l when just 7-1 for this race in 2023; long layoff before last season and easily best effort since was his 2m4f non-handicap win with first-time blinkers (kept since) at Clonmel last June; fell in August on his second chase start and unseated over hurdles in September; absent since and others have more pressing claims.

runners.comment: Progressive novice; second when hot favourite for a top 2m handicap at Leopardstown latest
runners.name: I Started A Joke
runners.spotlight: Reserve; 13th at 33-1 in the Champion Bumper here last March; progressing well at 2m in the mud as a hurdler, easily winning a maiden at Punchestown and second of 19 when hot favourite for a top handicap at Leopardstown on latest run; the front two drew clear in the latter, after this one travelled best and launched a strong challenge; not crying out for this longer trip on that display but his stable has made many notable strikes.

runners.comment: Returns to hurdling in first cheekpieces; next to no exposure in handicaps but low on list
runners.name: Intense Approach
runners.spotlight: Reserve; won four times (once on good here) as a novice hurdler last season before pulling up at 14-1 in the 3m Grade 1 novice event here; won chase debut at the Galway festival (2m6f) last August but chase career has gone badly the wrong way since, latest start 11 days ago; returns to hurdling in first-time cheekpieces; next to no exposure in handicaps but low on the list.

15:20.race_name: Glenfarclas Cross Country Chase (A Limited Handicap) (GBB Race)

runners.comment: 2-2 over C&D last season (including this race); won Czech marathon on sole start this term
runners.name: Stumptown
runners.spotlight: Dual C&D winner last season, latterly when beating Latenightpass by 7l in this race (good to soft; first-time cheekpieces); seen only once this term, landing prestigious Velka Pardubicka cross-country chase in Czech Republic (4m2f, good; back in cheekpieces) in October, and has a lofty handicap mark to overcome but still commands respect; blinkers back on today.

runners.comment: Won comfortably over C&D in January and is still unexposed in this discipline; big player
runners.name: Favori De Champdou
runners.spotlight: Fell mid-race here on cross-country debut in December but quickly bounced back when causing 66-1 shock in valuable handicap over regulation fences at Leopardstown's Christmas festival (3m, yielding) before winning comfortably by just over 8l returned to this C&D (soft) in January; still unexposed in this discipline; strong contender.

runners.comment: C&D winner in December and ran well for a long way on slower-than-ideal ground last time
runners.name: Final Orders
runners.spotlight: High-mileage 10yo who took very well to this C&D (good) in December, winning quite comfortably by just over 4l; weakened into fifth in soft-ground C&D contest won by Favori De Champdou in January but ran well for a long way and ought to be better suited by the less testing conditions today; each-way claims at least.

runners.breeder: S C E A Ecurie Haras Des Marais
runners.comment: Inconsistent nowadays but did very well to finish third in this race a year ago
runners.name: Vanillier
runners.spotlight: Thorough stayer who came second in the 2023 Grand National; not very consistent nowadays but did very well to finish third behind Stumptown in this race last year (good to soft), having lost ground when nearly taking the wrong course in early stages, and returns here after a win on Bank course at Punchestown (3m1f, soft to heavy) last month.

runners.comment: Regressive veteran; placed on Bank course at Punchestown last month but others appeal more
runners.name: Conflated
runners.spotlight: Top class over regulation fences in his prime (dual 3m Grade 1 winner) but has regressed and become inconsistent; gave a pretty good account when placed behind Vanillier on Bank course at Punchestown (3m1f, soft to heavy; refitted cheekpieces/first-time tongue-tie) last month but was well beaten on his only C&D start (in 2024); younger rivals appeal much more.

runners.comment: Ran quite well in major handicaps on last two starts; not ruled out on cross-country debut
runners.name: Pied Piper
runners.owner: Mrs M Roden & Mrs R Nolan
runners.spotlight: Gained all three chase wins in small-field novice events last April-June; not beaten far when ninth of 28 in valuable Leopardstown handicap won by Favori De Champdou over Christmas (3m, yielding; wore usual cheekpieces) and seemed to be running well when falling at third-last fence in the Thyestes at Gowran (3m1f, heavy; blinkered) in January; has stamina to prove on cross-country debut but not ruled out; cheekpieces back on today.

runners.comment: Respectable fourth at Punchestown when back under rules last month; much more needed here
runners.name: Fakir dOudairies
runners.spotlight: Four-time Grade 1 chase winner (2m4f-2m5f) for Joseph O'Brien but left that stable after a disappointing cross-country debut over C&D in December 2024; returned to racing under rules with respectable fourth behind Vanillier on Bank course at Punchestown (3m1f, soft to heavy) last month but a much bigger performance will be needed here.

runners.comment: Out of form since clear second in last season's Thyestes; cross-country debut
runners.name: Velvet Elvis
runners.spotlight: Peak form includes a clear second to subsequent Grand National winner Nick Rockett in Thyestes Chase at Gowran (3m1f, soft to heavy) for Gavin Cromwell in January 2025; well handicapped on that effort (even though 1lb wrong) but has looked out of sorts since (four runs; last three for this stable) and it takes a leap of faith to support him on this cross-country debut; wore cheekpieces for four of last five races; visor is tried today.

runners.comment: Untested over C&D but twice ran well on Bank course at Punchestown in 2025; considered
runners.name: Desertmore House
runners.owner: O B P Carroll & Anthony Vaughan
runners.spotlight: Untested on this track but close second in La Touche Cup on cross-country debut at Punchestown (4m1f, good to yielding) last May and looked in very good nick when beating The Goffer and Final Orders to win over 3m on that Bank course (soft to heavy) in November; pulled up over hurdles the following month and 3lb out of the weights today but still considered.

runners.comment: Very useful in Ireland in 2024 but looks too risky on this stable/cross-country debut
runners.name: Horantzau dAiry
runners.spotlight: Very useful handicap chaser for Willie Mullins in 2024 and placed for Michael Keady last spring (2m4f, good) but absent since pulled up for Sara Bradstock in September (bled from the nose); now with another new stable for cross-country debut; 4lb wrong; best to look elsewhere.

runners.comment: Pulled up in this race a year ago and also struggled on recent stable debut
runners.name: Minella Crooner
runners.spotlight: Very useful at his best for Gordon Elliott but was pulled up in this race last year and changed hands after a heavy defeat over regulation fences at Punchestown festival; struggled when dropped back to 2m4f for last month's stable debut; 6lb wrong here and has too much to prove.

runners.comment: C&D winner; second in this last year but out of form this season and long in the tooth now
runners.name: Latenightpass
runners.spotlight: Won over C&D (soft) in 2023 and a commendable second to Stumptown in this race last year (good to soft) but safely held in C&D races won by Final Orders and Favori De Champdou on his last two appearances and is getting long in the tooth now; 8lb out of the weights.

runners.comment: Stayed on for fourth in this race in 2025 but effectively 5lb higher this year
runners.name: The Goffer
runners.spotlight: Has made the frame at two Cheltenham Festivals, more recently when staying on from long way off the pace to take fourth behind Stumptown in this race in 2025 (good to soft); returns here after a pretty good second to Vanillier on Bank course at Punchestown (3m1f, soft to heavy) but, from out of the weights, is effectively 5lb higher than last year; sports first-time cheekpieces.

runners.comment: Out of form this season and makes cross-country debut from 11lb out of the handicap
runners.name: Famous Bridge
runners.spotlight: Very useful handicapper over regulation fences on his day and a very respectable sixth in last year's Ultima (3m1f, good to soft) at this meeting; won't fail through lack of stamina but has been out of form this season and makes cross-country debut from 11lb out of the handicap.

16:00.race_name: BetMGM Queen Mother Champion Chase (Grade 1) (GBB Race)

runners.comment: Placed in C&D handicap in the autumn; has the worst chance on ratings in this field
runners.name: Brookie
runners.spotlight: Lacked fluency and ran poorly at Ascot when last seen; ran creditably in C&D handicap the time before but that form is a long way below Champion Chase standard and he's comfortably held by Majborough on Punchestown festival running; has the worst chance on ratings.

runners.comment: Seems on the wane and looks far from sure to sustain his good record (213) in this race
runners.name: Captain Guinness
runners.spotlight: Has a good record (213) in the Champion Chase but is by no means certain to sustain it; proved a somewhat fortuitous winner of a weak edition two years ago (on soft ground) when the race fell apart and only three runners completed; far from solid on his form this term, below par in Grade 3 most recently, and returns to Cheltenham as an 11yo who may be on the wane; wears first-time headgear.

runners.comment: Weakened into last of five finishers in this contest last season; others preferred
runners.name: Found A Fifty
runners.spotlight: Fared best of the rest behind the impressive winner in the 2024 Arkle but weakened into last of five finishers in this contest last season and has largely fallen short at Grade 1 level in open company; beaten 19l by Majborough at this year's Dublin Racing Festival and flopped when back down in class at Navan (2m4f; blowing hard post race) later in February.

runners.breeder: E Clayeux & S C Ecurie Couderc
runners.comment: Faller last time and 0-3 at the Cheltenham Festival; otherwise a huge player on ratings
runners.name: Il Etait Temps
runners.spotlight: Acts on any ground; small in stature but big in talent and his record of 7-10 over fences features five Grade 1 wins, the most recent impressively in this season's Tingle Creek at Sandown; not bombproof in this scenario as he's 0-3 at the Cheltenham Festival (finishing positions 553) and was let down by his jumping in the 2024 Arkle, admittedly posting a good placed effort in the circumstances; possible denting of confidence is another concern as he was winded and took a while to get up from a late fall in the Clarence House most recently (under pressure and not responding when the tumble occurred); removal of usual hood adds to the uncertainty; otherwise a huge player provided he's in top form.

runners.comment: Ran very well in Grade 1 novice chase at Leopardstown last time; open to further progress
runners.name: Irish Panther
runners.spotlight: Very short on chasing experience, having raced just twice in this sphere, but by the same token looks open to any amount of further improvement despite being a 9yo (latecomer to this scene); close second, clear of remainder, in Grade 1 novice at Leopardstown (2m1f, yielding) when attempting to follow up his comfortable success in a Naas race that's worked out well; has shown good progress for current yard and looks interesting pitched into open company instead of bashing heads with similarly unexposed rivals in the Arkle.

runners.breeder: E A R L Du Moulin
runners.comment: Progressive in the main; easy winner of this season's Shloer over C&D; favourably fresh
runners.name: LEau du Sud
runners.owner: Mason Hogarth Ferguson Hales The Late J Hales
runners.spotlight: Progressive in the main; smart novice chaser last term and ties in closely with Majborough on Arkle bare form (good to soft; finished a close fourth); below par in the 2025 Tingle Creek when last seen but this looks the day to catch him; successful the last three times he has returned from a break of two months or bigger, most recently in this season's Shloer over C&D (soft) when easily beating his rivals and registering a fourth Graded win, as well as cementing his Champion Chase claims; favourably fresh and rightly respected.

runners.comment: In touch when falling in this race last year but needs to take his form to a new level
runners.name: Libberty Hunter
runners.spotlight: In touch and still going okay when falling three out in this race last year but it's difficult to ascertain where he'd have finished with a clear round; overall record at Cheltenham is 121FU, both wins in handicaps on the New course; ran creditably, one place behind Saint Segal, in the Game Spirit most recently; at the age of ten he's unlikely to find the major improvement that's needed on ratings.

runners.comment: Would have won last year's Arkle but for errors; impressive in the Dublin Chase; top rated
runners.name: Majborough
runners.spotlight: Talented youngster who triumphed in the Triumph at this meeting in 2024 and shaped like the best horse when close third in last year's Arkle, which he would likely have won but for late mistakes that included a howler two out; again lacked fluency when beaten twice in December but took very well to first-time cheekpieces and jumped better on his way to a highly impressive performance in the Dublin Chase at Leopardstown (2m1f, soft) since, beating 2025 Champion Chase winner Marine Nationale by 19l; good chance of following up in the retained headgear, provided the form is confirmed and a reversion to errors is avoided.

runners.comment: Running better than ever when final-fence faller in this race last year; absent since
runners.name: Quilixios
runners.spotlight: Landed the Triumph at this meeting in 2021 and was in the process of producing a career-best performance, albeit seeming likely to come off second best in the argument, when final-fence faller in this contest 12 months ago (good to soft); absent since but has a good reappearance record, allied with his proven ability to act very well at the Cheltenham Festival; another big run may be on the cards.

runners.breeder: E A R L Haras Du Mondant Et Al
runners.comment: Has become very consistent but faces a stiffer assignment upped further in class
runners.name: Saint Segal
runners.spotlight: Acts on any ground; has become a very consistent chaser; form figures this term read 12122, the second-place finishes in Grade 2 events, including handicaps; ran creditably behind a leading novice in the Game Spirit at Newbury most recently; even if he gives his running again, that won't be nearly enough to trouble the judge now that he is upped further in class; a lot to find.

16:40.race_name: Debenhams Johnny Henderson Grand Annual Challenge Cup Handicap Chase (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)

runners.comment: Conceding weight all round when runner-up in Grade 3 last time; not ruled out each-way
runners.name: Touch Me Not
runners.spotlight: Tailed off in last season's Arkle on sole visit here and has a lofty mark to defy; however, he won a Grade 2 novice chase last term and ran really well in second in a 2m Grade 3 at Naas recently when conceding 9lb to all of his rivals; James Smith removes 5lb; not ruled out each-way.

runners.comment: 10yo who has been better than ever this season (2-2 in handicaps); entitled to respect
runners.name: Calico
runners.spotlight: 10yo who has been better than ever this season, winning over C&D (good to soft) in October on his reappearance and following up at Ascot (2m1f, good to soft) in November, despite jumping to the left at that right-handed venue; heavy ground probably not ideal when respectable fourth of six in Grade 2 at Newbury last month; entitled to respect.

runners.breeder: B Decouz & S C E A Du Bas Bugey
runners.comment: Grade 2 novice chase winner last season; Grade 2 h'dle win this term but may be vulnerable
runners.name: Rubaud
runners.spotlight: Listed/Grade 2 wins over hurdles this term; goes back over fences for the first time since last May and he's 1-5 in this sphere, the win coming in a Grade 2 novice last February; sixth of 15 off this mark in the Scottish Champion Hurdle in April 2024 when he last tackled a handicap; may be vulnerable.

runners.breeder: S C E A Pa Ouvry & E A R L Ecurie Des
runners.comment: Running well in defeat in Graded races and has the potential to be better than this mark
runners.name: Be Aware
runners.spotlight: Improved form when winning on chase debut at Stratford (2m3f, good to soft) in October and strong performances when runner-up in Graded races on his three starts since, including over C&D (soft); this lightly raced 7yo is in top hands and has the potential to be better than this mark now back in a handicap; the hood is left off today, but he ran well without it in December.

runners.breeder: Mrs Tessa Greatrex & Mr D Futter
runners.comment: Fifth of 14 at Leopardstown last month and he's capable of building on that
runners.name: Inthepocket
runners.spotlight: Won Grade 1 Top Novices' Hurdle at Aintree (2m, good to soft) in April 2023; he's raced seven times since, all over fences, with just one win (a beginners chase in October 2024) and he can be difficult to settle; however, he took a step back in the right direction when fifth of 14 in a handicap at Leopardstown (2m1f, soft) last month and is capable of building on that.

runners.comment: Well handicapped on November 2024 C&D form but this 11yo hasn't shone this season
runners.name: Boothill
runners.spotlight: Ascot specialist who ran really well when second to Jonbon in C&D Grade 2 (good) in November 2024; well handicapped on that form but this 11yo has struggled to get competitive this season; wind op needs to prompt a revival.

runners.comment: Won big-field h'cap at Leopardstown in December; soft ground may not have been ideal since
runners.name: Addragoole
runners.spotlight: Switched to fences last August and he's been progressive, winning a competitive handicap at Leopardstown (2m1f, yielding) in December and solid third of 14 there (2m1f, soft) last month; today's likely return to better ground could be a plus and this 7yo remains open to further improvement; chance.

runners.breeder: J Magnien C Magnien & B Magnien
runners.comment: Below par this season but wind op since last time and he's 2-2 at the Cheltenham Festival
runners.name: Jazzy Matty
runners.spotlight: 8lb higher than when winning this last year (good to soft) and his subsequent form (chiefly over hurdles) hasn't been at the same level; however, he's had a wind op since last time and his 2-2 record at the Cheltenham Festival (also won the Fred Winter in 2023) means he's firmly in calculations.

runners.comment: Winter wins came in small fields but this lightly raced 7yo did it convincingly both times
runners.name: Vanderpoel
runners.spotlight: Won at Ascot (2m1f, soft) in December on third chase start and followed up at Sandown (1m7f, good) in January; those wins came in small fields and this is much more competitive, but this lightly raced 7yo did it convincingly both times and it remains to be seen where the ceiling of his ability lies.

runners.comment: Grade 3 novice win at Fairyhouse in January and could be suited by this big-field scenario
runners.name: Western Diego
runners.spotlight: Inconsistent and just one win from his eight chase starts but that came in a Grade 3 novice at Fairyhouse (2m1f, yielding) in January; weakened when fourth of 14 in handicap at Leopardstown (2m1f, soft) last month and today's forecast better ground could help; looks the type who may prove well suited by this big-field scenario; not discounted for top Irish stable.

runners.comment: Of interest on his win at Ayr last April but hard to fancy on winter evidence; yard debut
runners.name: The Other Mozzie
runners.spotlight: Won in good style for Gavin Cromwell at Ayr (2m, good to soft) last April and on that evidence this 3lb higher mark may not be beyond him; however, he was underwhelming on his final two runs for that yard and a major turnaround is needed on this stable debut, for which a tongue-tie goes on.

runners.breeder: M H Sly Dr T Davies & Mrs P Sly
runners.comment: Goes well fresh and he's in with an each-way shout on his form in the autumn
runners.name: Special Cadeau
runners.spotlight: 0-6 since winning on chase debut last February; below par at Fairyhouse in November last time but the yielding to soft ground provides an excuse; good runs at Roscommon (2m, good to yielding) and Ascot (2m1f, good) previously in the autumn and he goes well fresh; has an each-way shout.

runners.comment: On a competitive mark but he was soundly beaten on all four visits here
runners.name: Martator
runners.spotlight: Ascot specialist who was second there in November off today's mark and he was in contention when unseating five out at Sandown in January; however, good runs were scarce in 2025 and he's been soundly beaten on all four visits here; tenth in this last year; blinkers replace cheekpieces.

runners.comment: 5l win in 2m5f Summer Plate last July; stiff track and strong pace will help at this trip
runners.name: Ballysax Hank
runners.spotlight: 5l win in the Summer Plate at Market Rasen (2m5f, good) last July and went close in the American Grand National (2m5f, firm) in October; excuses on both winter starts (3m then soft ground); the drop back to 2m poses a question but the stiff track and strong pace will help; possible player.

runners.comment: Can make mistakes but has plenty of ability; could make bold bid if minimising the errors
runners.name: Personal Ambition
runners.spotlight: He's had jumping issues and should have won a Grade 2 novice chase at Ascot in December 2024 (2m3f, good to soft; bad mistake at final fence); beat just two rivals when getting off the mark in this sphere at Newbury (2m, soft) recently but that was still a very encouraging effort in first-time blinkers (retained); could make a bold bid if minimising the errors.

runners.breeder: E A R L Elevage De Busset
runners.comment: 3-4 over fences but today is a much tougher test of his credentials
runners.name: Jour dEvasion
runners.spotlight: 3-4 over fences, the wins coming over 2m1f/2m on heavy/good to soft; clearly knows how to get the job done and he's on an upward curve, but he's 5lb higher than for a narrow win in a small field at Warwick last time and today is a much tougher test of his credentials.

runners.comment: Hasn't kicked on following chase debut win but there could be some mileage in her mark
runners.name: Break My Soul
runners.spotlight: Has failed to kick on since chase debut win at Gowran Park (2m, heavy) in November; however, the best run of her career came when fourth of five finishers in the Grade 1 Aintree Hurdle (2m4f, good to soft) last April and on that evidence there could be some mileage in her mark; not written off.

runners.comment: Very good start to chasing career in October; could bounce back now back on better ground
runners.name: Relieved Of Duties
runners.spotlight: Won on chase debut at Fairyhouse (2m, yielding) in October and very creditable second in quality novice over this C&D (good to soft) 13 days later; well beaten both starts since but they have been on testing ground; could bounce back and play a leading role now he's back on a better surface.

runners.comment: 7l fifth in this last March; 5lb higher this time around but not discounted each-way
runners.name: Jasko Des Dames
runners.spotlight: 7l fifth in this last March (good to soft); runner-up on both starts in the autumn (including C&D) and soft ground may have been against him when down the field at Leopardstown (2m1f) last month; he's 5lb higher than 12 months ago but is not discounted each-way for his good Irish stable.

runners.comment: Improved form when runner-up on both starts this season and could have even more to offer
runners.name: Release The Beast
runners.spotlight: Second-season chaser who has shown improved form when runner-up on both starts this term, most recently second of 20 to Addragoole at Leopardstown (2m1f, yielding) in December; this unexposed 7yo could have even more to offer and might have a part to play; wears a first-time hood.

runners.comment: Reserve; 5l second of 14 in handicap at Leopardstown last month and he's not ruled out
runners.name: Golden Joy
runners.spotlight: Reserve; up and down since winning at Leopardstown (2m1f, yielding) last March on second chase start but returned to form with 5l second of 14 in handicap there (2m1f, soft) last month in first-time visor (retained); not ruled out.

runners.comment: Reserve; firm suspicion he's an improved performer this season and he's one to consider
runners.name: Ryans Rocket
runners.spotlight: Reserve; second-season chaser who won a shade cosily on reappearance at Newbury (2m, good to soft) in November and, although there was still a fair way to go, he was travelling nicely when unseating five out at Kempton (2m, good) in December; there is a firm suspicion he's an improved performer this season and he's one to consider.

17:20.race_name: Weatherbys Champion Bumper (In Memory Of Sir Johnny Weatherby) (A Standard Open NH Flat Race) (GBB)

runners.breeder: S Gesbert J Lacouture & C Moreau
runners.comment: Impressive in making all for both his bumper wins; trainer rates him very highly
runners.name: Bass Hunter
runners.spotlight: Not an instant success in Irish points but 2-2 in bumpers despite free-going tendencies evident in both; made all at Newbury (good to soft) and repeated the trick at Ascot (soft) where he was in splendid isolation for large parts of the race before predictably tiring late on; that form has taken a battering but he was much the best of that field; should similar tactics be employed, it may help that this race is often slowly run; highly regarded and much respected.

runners.comment: Easy winner last time but no match for It's Only A Game the run before
runners.name: Boycetown
runners.spotlight: Cost 120,000euros after finishing second in an Irish point; he took the field apart to win by clear daylight at Down Royal (yielding) but It's Only A Game comfortably had his measure the time before; this 5yo has him to worry about and others; tongue-tie added.

runners.comment: Beat some of these in an often-influential Grade 2 at Leopardstown last month
runners.name: Broadway Ted
runners.spotlight: Both runs on heavy; debut win was at Ayr and he followed up in the Grade 2 at the Dublin Racing Festival that's often a good guide to this (three horses have achieved the double since 2019); only a short head in front of With Nolimit and a suspicion that Charismatic Kid (third) and It's Only A Game (fourth) were not seen to best effect in behind, but this is a nice prospect.

runners.comment: Ran below market expectations in a Grade 2 last time; this drier ground could assist
runners.name: Charismatic Kid
runners.spotlight: Bought for £300,000 soon after winning a Navan bumper in early December; he took a tall reputation into the Grade 2 at Leopardstown in early February won by Broadway Ted and was backed accordingly, only for his effort to peter out after briefly threatening up the straight; could be capable of better on this surface (has raced on soft or heavy) but clearly needs to be.

runners.comment: A dual winner, but on all his form this looks three bridges too far
runners.name: Chicker
runners.spotlight: His wins at Worcester and here came on good ground, so perhaps the soft surface found him out when only sixth in a Listed race back here in November; however, on all his form, this looks three bridges too far.

runners.comment: Won easily at Ayr despite racing freely and wandering around when clear; now hooded
runners.name: Diamant Dore
runners.spotlight: Held every chance when falling late on in an Irish point for which he was odds-on; later recruited for £125,000; drew clear for a 17l success at Ayr (heavy), beating a previous winner; his RPR was encouraging enough to believe he might hold his own in this stronger company; raced freely at Ayr and wandered around when clear, so a hood is now fitted.

runners.breeder: Sarl Elevage Des Vallons & M Ian Kellit
runners.comment: Behind three of these in a Grade 2 but did get warm beforehand and wasn't ideally placed
runners.name: Its Only A Game
runners.spotlight: Much too good for Boycetown at Punchestown (soft to heavy; first run in a tongue-tie that's been retained) and, although his bubble was burst to some extent at Leopardstown (heavy), he did get noticeably warm beforehand and probably wasn't seen to best effect held up off modest fractions; can do better, and probably a lot better.

runners.comment: Posted a smart Topspeed figure (best in this race) when impressing at Leopardstown
runners.name: Keep Him Company
runners.spotlight: It was a timely point win last March as 12 days later he fetched £220,000 at the sales here on the eve of the Gold Cup; so far so good under rules having won both his bumpers, in the latest at Leopardstown (good to yielding) looking stronger the further he went (Topspeed figure sets the standard here); powerful owners have never prioritised this race but they might be warming to it having had the third two years ago (their best finish from nine runners) and the favourite last year; interesting.

runners.breeder: S C E A Du Moulin De Bel Oeuvre
runners.comment: Has a strikingly similar profile to the stable's 2024 winner Jasmin De Vaux; big shout
runners.name: Love Sign dAunou
runners.spotlight: Has a strikingly similar profile to the stable's 2024 winner Jasmin De Vaux, who also won a point winner before scooting home in the same Naas bumper (2m2f, heavy) that this 5yo won by 24l (made all; 5-4 favourite); perhaps he didn't beat a lot but it looked good and top connections committed to Cheltenham straight after; trainer has won this 14 times and it sounds as though this runner is right up the pecking order in his five-strong squad; Patrick Mullins rides; "could be anything" tag definitely applies here.

runners.comment: Looked good at Limerick; sure to win more races but this is unlikely to be one of them
runners.name: Of Land And Sea
runners.spotlight: Patrick Mullins has been aboard for all his three runs but isn't here; impressed at Limerick last time (heavy) and his RPR was nothing to be sniffed at, despite Mullins keeping so wide that he ventured onto an AW strip that circled the track; sure to win more races but this is unlikely to be one of them.

runners.comment: Flattered to get so close to Bass Hunter latest; no maiden has ever won this race
runners.name: Tally Ho Back
runners.spotlight: Flattered to finish a length behind the trailblazing Bass Hunter at Ascot and he was then a disappointing favourite at Windsor (again on soft); no maiden has ever won this race.

runners.comment: Won by 9l at Navan where Patrick Mullins barely pressed the accelerator pedal
runners.name: The Irish Avatar
runners.spotlight: Snapped up for £200,000 soon after finishing second in an Irish point last spring (winner absent since); reappeared in January for an all-the-way 9l victory on soft to heavy at Navan where Patrick Mullins barely pressed the accelerator pedal; that effort looks all the more striking now with the runner-up winning comfortably the following month; it's all guesswork in gauging how good he might be, but Mullins prefers Love Sign d'Aunou.

runners.comment: Well related and won a traditionally strong bumper at Leopardstown; top Flat rider booked
runners.name: The Mourne Rambler
runners.spotlight: Beaten in his only point; Noel Meade has done well with other members of the dam's family; it was a traditionally strong bumper he won at Leopardstown over Christmas (yielding) and he was extending his superiority at the line; a formline through the third puts this 5yo on a par with Keep Him Company; aided by the assistance of star Flat jockey Colin Keane, he's an intriguing runner.

runners.comment: Whether he possesses the required gears to mix it with the best of these is unlikely
runners.name: The Skecher
runners.spotlight: Ground it out from the front at Ayr (soft) when making a successful debut for Dan Skelton, who considers him a "big, galloping type"; whether he possesses the required gears to mix it with the best of these is unlikely.

runners.comment: Fairyhouse RPR was nothing special; probably lacks the star potential of some in here
runners.name: The Wager
runners.spotlight: Debut defeat was for a different yard; his narrow success at Fairyhouse (yielding) wasn't pretty and the RPR nothing to boast about; probably lacks the star potential of some in here and Patrick Mullins (aboard last time) presumably agrees.

runners.comment: Promising stayer in the making but looks comfortably held by Bass Hunter on Ascot form
runners.name: Vango Can Go
runners.spotlight: Second in a 3m Irish point on good to yielding; Charlie Todd has been aboard for both his bumpers (soft), when winning well at Southwell but then 5l behind Bass Hunter at Ascot where Tally Ho Back was also ahead of him; could reverse placings with the second but there's obvious no reason why he'll be any closer to the winner of that race.

runners.comment: Hit a flat spot at Huntingdon before staying on best; looks vulnerable
runners.name: Wildes Legacy
runners.spotlight: AW winner on debut and, in the end, comfortably defied a penalty on soft ground at Huntingdon, though he appeared to hit a flat spot before staying on better than the rest; will need to be a whole lot sharper here.

runners.comment: Just missed out to Broadway Ted in a Grade 2 latest; he's not his stable's main hope
runners.name: With Nolimit
runners.spotlight: With his dam closely related to a Welsh National winner, it was no surprise to see him finishing well when narrowly failing to reel in Broadway Ted in a Grade 2 at Leopardstown; useful but Gordon Elliott has made it clear that the same owner's Keep Him Company is the yard's principal hope.

runners.comment: Would have been second last time had the runner-up's rider not prematurely eased down
runners.name: Moonverrin
runners.spotlight: The 20-1 winner of a Grade 2 for mares at Leopardstown's Dublin Racing Festival and would probably have been second had the runner-up's rider not eased down prematurely; Bambino Fever won the same race en route to taking this last year, but this mare's claims are nothing like so convincing.

runners.comment: Not wildly impressive at Gowran but he's clearly open to any amount of improvement
runners.name: Our Trigger
runners.spotlight: Bred to be a Cheltenham horse as a brother to Arkle winner Gaelic Warrior; what he achieved in winning a four-runner bumper at Gowran (on heavy) is anyone's guess but he did go off odds-on and did it easily in the end having come under pressure turning for home; that performance didn't scream 'Champion Bumper winner' but he's clearly open to any amount of improvement; this can be a struggle for 4yos, however.

runners.comment: Won easily at Naas but only Cue Card has won as a 4yo since 1995
runners.name: Quiryn
runners.spotlight: Predominantly Flat bred but there are jumpers in the family; another unexposed Willie Mullins runner who won without a care in the world at Naas (soft) and he has the scope to get better; however, while ten previous winners of this had raced once, only Cue Card has won as a 4yo since 1995; Paul Townend rides.

runners.comment: Quality bumper form in France; bought for 710,000euros; 4yo filly with all the allowances
runners.name: Mets Ta Ceinture
runners.spotlight: Three runs in French bumpers at around 1m4f on ground ranging from good to soft to heavy (all in a tongue-tie that's now dispensed with); well on top for the wins and she was beaten by a smart prospect when close up in a Grade 2 in October; it took a whopping 710,000euros to secure her services and Harry Skelton prefers her over the stable's other two runners; she's a 4yo filly receiving all the allowances and three females have won this since 2017, albeit older ones.
